title: Who Counted
concept: A machine now reads a fish ear stone with light, and the film opens it up to find that every answer it gives was taught by people counting rings at microscopes, one ring at a time.

fingerprint.palette: warm golden lamp brass, pearl, near-infrared magenta over Bering teal
fingerprint.metaphor: A curve that turns out to be made of tally marks

palette: warm golden lamp brass, pearl, near-infrared magenta over Bering teal
divergence_note: September 30th was a fog slate table with a phone and a binder, and September 23rd was a ruled government statement at dusk. This film has no document pile. It lives in dark water, under one brass microscope lamp, inside a cutaway machine and in a 1930s timber hangar, and its hero is an organic stone with rings rather than a sheet of paper. The accent is a near-infrared magenta used only on the machine.

angle.thesis: NOAA's machine reader for Alaska groundfish ages is a real win, and it works because people at microscopes spent years counting annual growth rings on an archive of 2.5 million otolith pairs going back to the 1960s, so the human readers didn't get replaced by the model, they're what taught it.
angle.falsifiability: Wrong if a NOAA source shows the NIR models learned age with no human-aged otoliths behind them, the gain came from the spectrometer alone, or conventional ageing dropped out of the process.
supporting_facts: c3+c4 30,000+ aged a year by counting annual growth rings like tree rings
c7+c8+c9 NIR signatures tied to age by ML, 600 to 800 percent more efficient, conventional ageing still part of the process
c1+c2+c10+c18 2.5 million pairs since the 1960s; models trained on archive samples, 2023 trained and tested on 8,617 pollock otoliths
angle.counter_point: The spectroscopy and ML made the archive pay (c7,c8), engineers get full credit. Stock assessment use is the next step (c14), no machine age has set a catch limit, managers set limits (c15).
angle.second_movement: c12+c13 around 2 million pairs sat in a 1930s wooden airplane hangar, moved 2012 on an NSF grant. Act 1 sells speed; the hangar shows speed is a payout on slow careful storage and counting.
angle.test_scene: THE NEXT STEP: a faster age only helps once it changes the numbers managers use, and NOAA puts assessment use ahead (c14); the microscope reader stays (c9); limits stay a human decision (c15). Concede, then: the win is real today as capacity and method.
angle.story_question: Where did the machine that ages Alaska's fish get its intelligence?

runner_ups.why_lost: implies a downstream result c8 doesn't show; lives on as Act 1 capacity beat
undersells a real win; becomes the Act 3 test scene

treatment.why: Strongest arc and the only turn that shows the thesis: the machine signature resolves into tally ticks. Fewest sets.
grafts: EXPLAINER rockfish cold open compressed to move by 1.3s
EXPLAINER question mark in the AGE OUT slot
treatment.judge_reasoning: Scorer: DRAMATIST 45, EXPLAINER 44, COMEDIAN 39, ENTHUSIAST 35. The Dramatist pitch had the strongest emotional arc and the most buildable set list; its static cold open is replaced by the Explainer moving rockfish.

hook.frame1: A rockfish glides through dark Aleutian water toward camera.
hook.headline: A FISH BORN IN 1878. WHO COUNTED?
hook.loopback: The button ends on the same ear stone and cuts to the same rockfish gliding.

open_loop.what: Who counted? The machine AGE OUT slot answer flips to the reader handwritten tag.

open_loop_2.what: The lit door at the end of the tagging room labelled STOCK ASSESSMENT. The same door waits above the dashed step, stamped NEXT STEP.

states.state: first click 0001, locked to the first ring pulse
steaming at the 30,000 a year pace
its digits copied onto the paper age tags that ride into the hopper
the training count lands on a readout styled as the same brass counter, 8,617
still clicking across the hall from the staircase
final click on counted reads 0144, the rings ripple, the loop

reveals.what: one stone becomes trays piling up behind the reader, 30,000+ a year
the bench wall falls away to 2.5 million pairs to a vanishing point
machine and reader share the bench as the signature builds back into tally ticks
